variables.name: buffer
variables.comment:
* This version only supports fully buffered DER.  This is easy to
     * work with, though if large objects are manipulated DER becomes
     * awkward to deal with.  That's where BER is useful, since BER
     * handles streaming data relatively well.

variables.name: tag
variables.comment: The DER tag of the value; one of the tag_ constants.

methods.name: private void init(byte[] data, int offset, int len, boolean allowIndefiniteLength) throws IOException
methods.comment: * private helper routine

methods.name: public DerInputStream subStream(int len, boolean do_skip) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Creates a new DER input stream from part of this input stream.
     *
     * @param len how long a chunk of the current input stream to use,
     *          starting at the current position.
     * @param do_skip true if the existing data in the input stream should
     *          be skipped.  If this value is false, the next data read
     *          on this stream and the newly created stream will be the
     *          same.

methods.name: public byte[] toByteArray()
methods.comment:
* Return what has been written to this DerInputStream
     * as a byte array. Useful for debugging.

methods.name: public int getInteger() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get an integer from the input stream as an integer.
     *
     * @return the integer held in this DER input stream.

methods.name: public BigInteger getBigInteger() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get a integer from the input stream as a BigInteger object.
     *
     * @return the integer held in this DER input stream.

methods.name: public BigInteger getPositiveBigInteger() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Returns an ASN.1 INTEGER value as a positive BigInteger.
     * This is just to deal with implementations that incorrectly encode
     * some values as negative.
     *
     * @return the integer held in this DER value as a BigInteger.

methods.name: public int getEnumerated() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get an enumerated from the input stream.
     *
     * @return the integer held in this DER input stream.

methods.name: public byte[] getBitString() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get a bit string from the input stream. Padded bits (if any)
     * will be stripped off before the bit string is returned.

methods.name: public BitArray getUnalignedBitString() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get a bit string from the input stream.  The bit string need
     * not be byte-aligned.

methods.name: public byte[] getOctetString() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Returns an ASN.1 OCTET STRING from the input stream.

methods.name: public void getBytes(byte[] val) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Returns the asked number of bytes from the input stream.

methods.name: public void getNull() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Reads an encoded null value from the input stream.

methods.name: public ObjectIdentifier getOID() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Reads an X.200 style Object Identifier from the stream.

methods.name: public DerValue[] getSequence(int startLen, boolean originalEncodedFormRetained) throws IOException
methods.comment: BEGIN Android-changed: Original encoded form needed for APKs parsing/validation.

methods.name: public DerValue[] getSequence(int startLen) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Return a sequence of encoded entities.  ASN.1 sequences are
     * ordered, and they are often used, like a "struct" in C or C++,
     * to group data values.  They may have optional or context
     * specific values.
     *
     * @param startLen guess about how long the sequence will be
     *          (used to initialize an auto-growing data structure)
     * @return array of the values in the sequence

methods.name: public DerValue[] getSet(int startLen) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Return a set of encoded entities.  ASN.1 sets are unordered,
     * though DER may specify an order for some kinds of sets (such
     * as the attributes in an X.500 relative distinguished name)
     * to facilitate binary comparisons of encoded values.
     *
     * @param startLen guess about how large the set will be
     *          (used to initialize an auto-growing data structure)
     * @return array of the values in the sequence

methods.name: public DerValue[] getSet(int startLen, boolean implicit) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Return a set of encoded entities.  ASN.1 sets are unordered,
     * though DER may specify an order for some kinds of sets (such
     * as the attributes in an X.500 relative distinguished name)
     * to facilitate binary comparisons of encoded values.
     *
     * @param startLen guess about how large the set will be
     *          (used to initialize an auto-growing data structure)
     * @param implicit if true tag is assumed implicit.
     * @return array of the values in the sequence

methods.name: public DerValue[] getSet(int startLen, boolean implicit, boolean originalEncodedFormRetained) throws IOException
protected DerValue[] readVector(int startLen) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Read a "vector" of values ... set or sequence have the
     * same encoding, except for the initial tag, so both use
     * this same helper routine.

methods.name: protected DerValue[] readVector(int startLen, boolean originalEncodedFormRetained) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Read a "vector" of values ... set or sequence have the
     * same encoding, except for the initial tag, so both use
     * this same helper routine.

methods.name: public DerValue getDerValue() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get a single DER-encoded value from the input stream.
     * It can often be useful to pull a value from the stream
     * and defer parsing it.  For example, you can pull a nested
     * sequence out with one call, and only examine its elements
     * later when you really need to.

methods.name: public String getUTF8String() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a UTF8String DER value.

methods.name: public String getPrintableString() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a PrintableString DER value.

methods.name: public String getT61String() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a T61String DER value.

methods.name: public String getIA5String() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a IA5tring DER value.

methods.name: public String getBMPString() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a BMPString DER value.

methods.name: public String getGeneralString() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Read a string that was encoded as a GeneralString DER value.

methods.name: private String readString(byte stringTag, String stringName, String enc) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Private helper routine to read an encoded string from the input
     * stream.
     * @param stringTag the tag for the type of string to read
     * @param stringName a name to display in error messages
     * @param enc the encoder to use to interpret the data. Should
     * correspond to the stringTag above.

methods.name: public Date getUTCTime() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Get a UTC encoded time value from the input stream.

methods.name: public Date getGeneralizedTime() throws IOException
methods.comment: * Get a Generalized encoded time value from the input stream.

methods.name: static int getLength(InputStream in) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Get a length from the input stream, allowing for at most 32 bits of
     * encoding to be used.  (Not the same as getting a tagged integer!)
     *
     * @return the length or -1 if indefinite length found.
     * @exception IOException on parsing error or unsupported lengths.

methods.name: public void mark(int value)
methods.comment: * Mark the current position in the buffer, so that * a later call to reset will return here.

methods.name: public void reset()
methods.comment: * Return to the position of the last mark * call. A mark is implicitly set at the beginning of * the stream when it is created.

methods.name: public int available()
methods.comment:
* Returns the number of bytes available for reading.
     * This is most useful for testing whether the stream is
     * empty.
